passages.title: Le matin de Julie
passages.blurb: A rushed morning, start to finish: present tense, reflexive verbs and the three families of article.

passages.title: Au marché
passages.blurb: A shopping list at the market: articles, quantities with de, and numbers up to a hundred.

passages.title: La chambre de Théo
passages.blurb: One small room, described from the window to under the bed: il y a, place prepositions, adjective agreement and possessives.

passages.title: Le week-end de Sarah
passages.blurb: A quiet Saturday that does not stay quiet: the passé composé with both auxiliaries, plus the connectors that order a story.

passages.title: Le message
passages.blurb: A text from an unknown number: the futur simple, the three ways of asking a question, and the whole ne … family.

passages.title: Chez le médecin
passages.blurb: A tired man, a waiting room and an awkward question: reflexive verbs, negation, object pronouns and il y a.

passages.title: Le dernier train
passages.blurb: A delayed night train, a father's old story, and a stranger who knew him. Imparfait against passé composé, and the four relative pronouns.

passages.title: La colocataire
passages.blurb: Two candidates for a spare room, one week of hesitation, and one phone call too late. Conditionnel, the three si-clauses, y and en, and comparatives.

passages.title: L'entretien
passages.blurb: A job interview conducted in two languages at once: what is said aloud, and what is thought. Subjunctive triggers, verbs with à and de, on and the passive, and register from soutenu to familier.

passages.title: La lettre de 1974
passages.blurb: An unsent letter in the bottom drawer, and a second handwriting at the foot of the last page. Plus-que-parfait, reported speech, participe présent, and lequel after prepositions.

passages.title: I. L'héritage
passages.blurb: Chapter one of ten. A notary's letter arrives in Lyon about an aunt Adrien had almost forgotten: the passé composé against the imparfait, possessives, and the whole ne … family.

passages.title: II. La rue Lepic
passages.blurb: Chapter two of ten. Adrien goes up the hill to the flat that is now his, and someone opens the door from the inside: prepositions, y and en, adjectives, and questions.

passages.title: III. Madame Berthier
passages.blurb: Chapter three of ten. Over two cups of coffee, a stranger describes the aunt Adrien never knew: the imparfait as portrait, and qui, que, où and dont doing the joining.

passages.title: IV. Ce qu'Odile avait fait
passages.blurb: Chapter four of ten. The notary lays out a document signed in 1998 and the inheritance changes shape: the plus-que-parfait, the past behind the past, plus dates and legal precision.

passages.title: V. Si j'avais su
passages.blurb: Chapter five of ten. Adrien and his sister argue about money down a bad phone line: the conditionnel, all three si-clause patterns, and what people say they would have done.

passages.title: VI. Il faut que
passages.blurb: Chapter six of ten. A lawyer explains what Adrien is entitled to do, and his mother explains what he ought to do: the subjunctive and its triggers, on both sides of an argument.

passages.title: VII. La boîte en fer
passages.blurb: Chapter seven of ten. Françoise opens a biscuit tin of letters and thirty years get reported in the past: discours indirect, the tense push-back, and the pronouns that shift with it.

passages.title: VIII. Ce dont personne ne parlait
passages.blurb: Chapter eight of ten. Adrien reads a 1998 letter his grandmother did send, and the family sentence is finally quoted: ce qui / ce que / ce dont, lequel after prepositions, on, and restriction with ne … que.

passages.title: IX. Elle aura tout prévu
passages.blurb: Chapter nine of ten. A second document surfaces at the notary's and Adrien works out what Odile planned: futur antérieur as supposition, infinitif passé, and the three things that end in -ant.

passages.title: X. Au fur et à mesure
passages.blurb: Chapter ten of ten. A year of Saturdays, one signature, and a paragraph in a printed book: durations with depuis, pendant and il y a, comparatives, exclamations, and a first taste of the passé simple.
